That way you can still enjoy South Asian community fairs or open-air cultural festivals in London without feeling uncomfortable.
(b) Since spring pollen can set off your seasonal allergic rhinitis, try planning outdoor time for late afternoons when counts are often lower, and wear wraparound sunglasses to keep pollen out of your eyes. A light scarf or mask can also help during peak blooms so you can still enjoy walks along Regent’s Canal or in leafy parks without discomfort.
(c) To enjoy the outdoors in spring, try going out in the late afternoon when conditions are milder and wear sunglasses to reduce glare. A light scarf or mask can also help if the air feels dusty, letting you make the most of parks, waterfronts, or neighbourhood walks.
(d) Because you tend to get mild hay fever in spring, you might enjoy outdoor activities later in the day when pollen levels have dropped. Pair that with sunglasses and a breathable face covering, and you can still relish canal strolls or garden visits without your allergies cutting them short.
